ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rhombus $ABCD$, $\angle D=120^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle 1$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given rhombus $ABCD$,\\
it follows that $AB\parallel CD$ and $\angle 1=\frac{1}{2}\angle DAB$,\\
since $\angle D=120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle DAB=60^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle 1=\frac{1}{2}\angle DAB=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: ABCD is drawn as a rhombus with D at the top, B at the bottom, A on the left, C on the right, and diagonal AC drawn horizontally. The marked angle 1 is the angle at A between side AD and diagonal AC, i.e. ∠DAC. From the text, use that ABCD is a rhombus and ∠D = 120°. In a rhombus, adjacent interior angles are supplementary, so ∠DAB = 180° − 120° = 60°. Also, each diagonal of a rhombus bisects the angles at its endpoints, so diagonal AC bisects ∠DAB. Therefore ∠1 = ∠DAC = 60°/2 = 30°.
